title: Tide gauges show altimetry about 10 mm above gauges after 2015, but the excess came before the 2019-2021 sea-level budget gap and changes by region, so it does not confirm an altimeter drift
abstract: Question: a prior result (sci:sha256:85ce0e95) found that altimetry was 6-9 mm above Argo steric plus GRACE-FO ocean mass in 2020.5-2024.0. Is this gap a drift of the reference altimeters (Jason-3, Sentinel-6MF)? Approach: we compared CMEMS DUACS gridded monthly sea level (0.125 degree, 1993-2026) with 514 PSMSL tide gauges (66S-66N, inverse-barometer corrected), fitted altimetry minus gauge on 2005-2015 per gauge to remove linear land motion, and averaged the anomalies over 113 ten-degree cells. Results: altimetry minus gauge in 2020.5-2024.0 was +10.4 mm (95% CI 1.2-20.0; time-noise null p 0.02), the size of the budget gap; 11 method variants gave +1.8 to +13.0 mm. But the timing does not agree: the excess was already +7.1 mm in 2016-2017.5 and +14.1 mm in 2018.5-2020, when the budget residual was 1-3 mm. From 2018.5-2020 to 2020.5-2024 the gap grew 4.0-5.8 mm, but altimetry minus gauge changed -3.7 mm (CI -9.1 to 1.6; p 0.02 under a gap-matching drift; the C3S two-satellite product gave -0.3 mm, not decisive). The excess is not a common offset: regional medians range from -38 mm (other extratropical gauges, n 23) and -14 mm (North America east and Gulf) to +16 mm (tropics), and the 197 GNSS-paired gauges gave +1.8 mm (+5.4 mm after GNSS correction). At the gauge cells altimetry stayed near its own trend; the gauges fell below theirs. A placebo moved 9 years earlier gave -11.6 mm, so excursions of this size also occur without a drift. Conclusion: tide gauges do not confirm an altimeter drift as the cause of the budget gap. Limitations: network noise is about 5 mm for a 3.5-year window, so a drift of about 1 mm/yr is not excluded; gridded, not along-track, altimetry; most gauges are in Europe, North America, Japan and Australia; timing tests and the regional split were chosen after the first result.

display.caption: 12-month means of altimetry minus tide gauge (CMEMS all-satellite and C3S two-satellite, 514 gauges, relative to a 2005-2015 fit) and of two sea-level budget residuals rebuilt with the method of 85ce0e95. The altimetry-minus-gauge excess appears in 2015-2018, before the budget residual grows in 2019.5-2021.

Altimetry minus gauge in W3 (2020.5-2024.0) and its change from W2 and W1, for 11 method variants, with 95% cell-bootstrap CIs. Shaded: range of the budget residual. The level agrees with the gap; the W2-to-W3 change does not.
Per-gauge altimetry-minus-gauge anomaly in 2020.5-2024.0 and regional medians. The sign changes between regions, which a common altimeter drift cannot explain.
